summary.one-line: Kavach is a merchant-side trust layer for agentic commerce: it verifies AI agents arriving at checkout (INBOUND / "Gate") and governs AI agents moving money out of a merchant's account (OUTBOUND / "Rail"), emitting hash-chained, replayable proof of every decision either way.
summary.thesis: Two questions nothing in the current agentic-payments stack asks: INBOUND — is the agent at the till the one this signed mandate delegates to, and does its cart match what the principal actually authorised (not just how much)? OUTBOUND — is this new intent financially the SAME OBLIGATION as money already in flight? Existing controls (Razorpay idempotency keys, AP2 mandates, Stripe Issuing caps, UPI Reserve Pay, MCP --read-only) all bound a REPLAY or an AMOUNT. None bounds a semantically new intent that is financially a duplicate, and none bounds WHAT a delegated agent buys. Canonical line used throughout the repo: "an idempotency key protects a retried request; nothing protects a re-decided one."
summary.second-thesis: A rail state and an obligation state are different things and must never be collapsed into one `status` field. Razorpay marks a refund "processed" before the ARN/RRN arrives from the gateway; the customer may not be credited for 5–10 business days. An agent that reads `status == "processed"` and reports "done" is wrong. truth.py returns both states plus the events that justify them, and refuses to emit a state no event supports.
summary.context: Hackathon/portfolio project targeting Razorpay (Indian PA/PG). Submitted under "Track 05 (Open)" but written in Track 01's quality-bar vocabulary (ADR-012). Currency is INR only; all money is integer minor units (paise). Language: Python 3.11+ backend, TypeScript/Next.js 16 frontend (static export). Datastore: SQLite (WAL). Default runtime mode is `replay` (a recorded Razorpay cassette); `live` is opt-in.

core-invariants.i: Nothing below a layer may import anything above it. Order (strongest guarantee first): eventlog → truth → ledger → intelligence → governor → mcp/http. Enforced socially (CONTRIBUTING.md), not mechanically (ADR-015).
A fact with no event behind it is structurally impossible. truth.derive() raises on an empty event list and every FinancialFact carries a non-empty `evidence` list of event seqs.

A learned model may only ever move a decision toward MORE caution. It never determines state, amount, authorisation or admission (ADR-004, ADR-006). A missing model RAISES the floor (outbound: risk not assessed; inbound: no ALLOW is reachable at all).

No float touches money anywhere. Amounts are integer minor units named `*_minor` end-to-end, including across the HTTP boundary and into the frontend; division to rupees happens once, at render time (web/lib/format.ts).

There is exactly ONE decision path. MCP, HTTP and the demo seeder all call `services/`. A "just for the dashboard" evaluator is explicitly forbidden — the seed refuses to stage an execution the governor did not allow, so a screenshot of the console is a screenshot of the system's behaviour.
Derived numbers are recomputed, never stored. Cumulative mandate spend, open exposure, and every dashboard tile are queries. A counter column would be a second copy that drifts (ADR-016).

Decisions are pure functions of (events, now, policy). Nothing reads the wall clock during a derivation; `now` is always passed in. This is what makes a decision replayable to the same verdict months later during a dispute.
The frontend never invents data — no fallback object, no `?? 0`. An unreachable API renders an error state, because zeros in a payments dashboard get believed.

table.name: events
table.columns: seq INTEGER PK AUTOINCREMENT · source TEXT (webhook | api_response | poll | agent_intent | seed | gate | governor | review) · external_id TEXT · entity_type TEXT (payment | refund | order | payout | intent | mandate) · entity_id TEXT · parent_entity_id TEXT NULL (payment_id for a refund; target_id for an intent) · event_type TEXT (refund.processed, api.create_refund, governor.decided.deny, gate.admitted, review.approved …) · payload TEXT (raw JSON, json.dumps(sort_keys=True), never mutated) · occurred_at INTEGER (epoch s, from the source) · received_at INTEGER (epoch s, when we saw it) · sig_verified INTEGER 0/1 (HMAC checked, for webhooks) · previous_event_hash TEXT NULL · event_hash TEXT · UNIQUE (source, external_id)
table.indexes: idx_events_entity(entity_type, entity_id, occurred_at, seq); partial idx_events_parent(parent_entity_id) WHERE NOT NULL
table.hash-formula: sha256( previous_event_hash? || "source:external_id:entity_type:entity_id:event_type:payload:occurred_at:sig_verified" || parent_entity_id? ) — payload is the exact stored JSON string with sorted keys; parent_entity_id is appended only when present. proof.py deliberately re-implements this rather than calling append()'s helper, so a disagreement between writer and verifier is itself the finding.
table.idempotency: append() is INSERT OR IGNORE inside a SAVEPOINT and returns (seq, is_new). A redelivered webhook is harmless.
table.ordering: for_entity() orders by (occurred_at, seq), NOT arrival — Razorpay webhooks do arrive out of order and a state machine fed arrival order walks backwards.
table.connection: connect(path, same_thread=True) opens WAL, foreign_keys=ON, isolation_level=None (autocommit) and applies the schema. `same_thread=False` is only for callers that give each unit of work its own connection (the HTTP API).

data-model.table:
intent_id TEXT PK · agent_id · session_id (a NEW session is exactly how a duplicate is born) · tool · target_type (payment|order) · target_id · amount_minor INTEGER · reason_text TEXT · created_at INTEGER · status TEXT · decision TEXT (JSON snapshot) · result_id TEXT NULL. Index on (target_type, target_id, created_at).
PROPOSED · APPROVED · EXECUTED · FAILED · "ESCALATE" (ESCALATED constant) · "DENY" (DENIED constant). REVIEW_STATUSES = ("ESCALATE",); REFUSED_STATUSES = ("DENY",); UNRESOLVED_STATUSES = ("APPROVED","FAILED") — the reconciler's queue.
ledger.record() raises ValueError on a duplicate intent_id: history is immutable. The mutable `decision` column is why decisions are ALSO written as hash-chained events — a decision that lives only here is a decision nobody can prove.
key_id TEXT PK, public_key BLOB (raw 32-byte Ed25519). Configured out of band; never self-asserted by the envelope.
nonce TEXT PK, mandate_id, claimed_at — claimed once, forever.
mandate_id TEXT PK, revoked_at, reason — read at decision time, never cached ("a cached revocation list is a revocation that does not work").
data-model.derived-object: entity_type, entity_id, rail_state (Rail), confidence (Confidence), obligation_open bool, amount_minor int, currency, reason (one sentence of why), evidence list[int] (event seqs, never empty), as_of, unresolved_for (seconds since the last state-changing event), arn (bank reference; the strongest credit signal observable). `to_agent()` is the agent-facing shape — deliberately has no field that can be read as "done" when it is not; it exposes `obligation: OPEN|CLOSED` and `settled_to_customer: bool(arn) and not obligation_open`.

module.name: pkg/kavach/money.py
module.purpose: The only money parser. Floats never touch the money path.
module.api: parse_inr(str|int|float|Decimal) -> int minor units. Rejects: bool (explicitly, because bool subclasses int), non-finite, negative, fractional paise, and anything above MAX_MINOR_UNITS = 100_000_000_00 (₹100 crore). Raises MoneyError (subclass of ValueError). format_inr(int) -> "1234.56" string; TypeErrors on non-int.
module.property-tests: tests/test_properties.py uses hypothesis over float inputs.

module.name: pkg/kavach/truth.py
module.enums: Rail = INITIATED | ACCEPTED | PROCESSING | CONFIRMED | SETTLED | FAILED_TERMINAL | REVERSED | AMBIGUOUS (all observable from Razorpay's position; NPCI/issuer-side conditions collapse to AMBIGUOUS with a stated reason — ADR-003) Confidence = DERIVED_CERTAIN (a signature-verified event states it directly) | DERIVED_PROBABLE (inferred, or from an unverified source) | UNKNOWN (contradicted, or stale past tolerance)
module.status-maps: _REFUND: created→ACCEPTED, pending→PROCESSING, processed→PROCESSING, failed→FAILED_TERMINAL _PAYMENT: created→INITIATED, authorized→ACCEPTED, captured→CONFIRMED, refunded→REVERSED, failed→FAILED_TERMINAL _RANK (INITIATED0 ACCEPTED1 PROCESSING2 CONFIRMED3 SETTLED4) exists ONLY to detect regression: a later event ranking lower than an earlier one is a CONTRADICTION, not an update, and collapses the fact to AMBIGUOUS/UNKNOWN with obligation_open=True. _STALE_SECONDS = {refund: 6h, payment: 15m}; default 1h. _TERMINAL = {FAILED_TERMINAL, REVERSED, SETTLED, CONFIRMED}. CONFIRMED's membership was a live bug when absent: a captured payment aged into AMBIGUOUS after 15 minutes, so the governor read payment_captured=False and DENIED every refund on any older payment.
module.derive-algorithm: derive(events, *, now) folds events in causal order. For each event it reads the entity body (`payload.<entity>.entity` for webhooks, flat for API responses), maps `status`, appends the event seq to `evidence`, tracks last_change, and lifts amount/currency/arn. Confidence is set per event: DERIVED_CERTAIN iff sig_verified else DERIVED_PROBABLE. Then, in order: 1. contradiction → AMBIGUOUS/UNKNOWN/open. 2. `credited` shortcut: a refund in PROCESSING carrying an ARN is credited. This is checked BEFORE the staleness rule, otherwise credited refunds age into AMBIGUOUS and open exposure grows forever (Razorpay sends no further event after 'processed'). 3. staleness: non-terminal, not credited, and unresolved > tolerance → AMBIGUOUS. 4. THE load-bearing judgement — refund obligation_open = NOT (PROCESSING AND arn). 'processed' without an ARN is DISPATCH, not CREDIT. With an ARN the state is re-labelled CONFIRMED and the obligation closes. FAILED_TERMINAL closes the obligation too (no credit will occur on that refund). For payments: obligation_open = state in {INITIATED, ACCEPTED}.

module.name: pkg/kavach/ledger.py
module.functions: init(conn) · record(conn, Intent, decision) — write-ahead, durable BEFORE execution · settle(conn, intent_id, status, result_id=None) · prior_intents(target_type, target_id) — everything ANY agent asked for against this target, in ANY session · fact_for(entity_type, entity_id, now) — derive or None · open_obligations(now) over MONEY_ENTITIES = (payment, refund, order, payout) · open_against_payment(payment_id, now) — reads the refund→payment link back out of the log (parent_entity_id) rather than keeping a second copy · exposure(payment_id, now) — open refund amounts PLUS EXECUTED intents whose result_id is not among the refunds we hold any event for. That extra term is the webhook-lag window where a naive agent double-refunds; the observed-set check prevents double counting.

module.name: pkg/kavach/governor.py
module.policy: Policy(allow_write=True, max_auto_refund_minor=1_000_00 (₹1,000), session_cap_minor=5_000_00, daily_cap_minor=25_000_00, risk_threshold=0.5, kill_switch=from KAVACH_KILL_SWITCH). Frozen dataclass; there is deliberately NO API that edits it ("a limit an operator can raise from the screen it is failing on is not a limit"). Callers that have a trained model construct Policy(risk_threshold=model.threshold) — the estimator's frozen train threshold.
module.actions: Action = ALLOW | ESCALATE (queued for a human; not a refusal) | DENY (never executable; no human waves it through here).
module.authority-order: 1. Accounting invariants → DENY, first and unarguable: · payment not captured → "there are no funds to refund" · exposure + amount > payment_amount → refunds may not exceed the captured amount 2. Permission tier → DENY if not policy.allow_write 3. Kill switch → ESCALATE (deliberately not DENY: halting agents must not strand a legitimate refund, it must put a human in front of it) 4. Truth-plane confidence → ESCALATE if any open obligation on this payment is UNKNOWN ("we cannot assert what we would be duplicating") 5. Duplicate-risk model → ESCALATE if risk_score >= policy.risk_threshold. ESCALATE ONLY. 6. Exposure caps → ESCALATE on per-refund limit, session cap, daily cap _escalate() never downgrades a DENY; _deny() replaces the reason list outright. A clean pass yields ALLOW with "no open obligation matches this intent and all caps are satisfied".
module.decision-shape: Decision{action, reasons[], evidence[] (event seqs from the truth plane), risk_score, risk_explain[], exposure_minor}; to_dict() renames to {action, reasons, evidence_events, duplicate_risk, risk_factors, open_exposure (rupees)}.
module.execution-split: reserve(conn, intent, decision) — must run inside BEGIN EXCLUSIVE. Records the intent + decision; ALLOW settles to APPROVED and returns {"executed": False, "reserved": True}. execute_provider(conn, client, intent, decision) — the external call, deliberately separate so the DB lock is released first. Sends idempotency_key = f"kavach-{intent_id}". On RazorpayError: FAILED if not retriable, else left APPROVED (the reconciler's job). On any other exception: FAILED, then re-raise — an obligation is never leaked. On success: EXECUTED with result_id = refund id. new_intent(...) is the refund-shaped helper; new_gate_intent(...) takes an arbitrary tool/target.

kavach-context.module: scan(conn) walks the whole chain once and returns {ok, events, checked, broken_at, detail, head}. verify_event_chain → (bool, human message). verify_range(seqs) answers whether cited events sit inside the verified prefix (a single event cannot be verified alone). chain(limit, before) returns a newest-first window with per-row `verified` plus `status` and `claims()`. claims() ships with every proof response so the UI cannot overstate by omission: proves — the ordered log has not been altered since it was written (SHA-256, chained) does_not_prove — WHO wrote an event (that is the webhook HMAC, recorded as sig_verified) limit — an attacker with write access could rewrite the chain from the edit forward; externally anchoring the head would close that and is NOT implemented.

stdlib BaseHTTPRequestHandler on POST /webhooks/razorpay. Requires X-Razorpay-Signature; verifies HMAC-SHA256 over the RAW body with RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET (constant-time, fail-closed on missing secret/signature). Then parses, derives entity_type from the event name prefix, extracts payload[entity_type].entity.id, sets parent_entity_id from entity.payment_id for refunds, and appends with sig_verified=True, external_id from X-Razorpay-Event-Id (falling back to "webhook:{id}:{event}") — so redelivery is idempotent. 401 missing/invalid signature · 400 malformed · 500 ingest failure · 200 OK.

reconcile_pending_intents(conn, client, tolerance_seconds=60, now=None): finds intents in status APPROVED older than the cutoff, fetches client.payment_refunds(target_id), and matches on notes.intent_id (which governor.execute_provider writes). Match → settle EXECUTED with the refund id; no match → settle FAILED. Only handles tool == "create_refund" and target_type == "payment"; anything else logs a warning and is skipped. The worker loops on --interval (default 30s) with --tolerance (default 60s).

Two modes. `live` performs real HTTPS calls (Basic auth, 15s timeout) and RECORDS every interaction to data/cassette.jsonl, so `replay` is a recording of reality rather than a mock written to agree with us. Replay is SEQUENTIAL, not keyed: identical repeated calls are the entire point of this project, and a keyed cache would collapse the naive agent's two refunds into one and hide the bug. Path comparison is structural (`_shape` replaces pay_/rfnd_/order_/plink_ ids with <id>) so a re-recorded cassette still replays. Endpoints: create_order, create_payment_link, fetch_payment, fetch_payments, fetch_refund, payment_refunds, create_refund(payment_id, amount_minor, idempotency_key ≥10 chars, notes). RazorpayError carries .status/.body/.path and .retriable (5xx or 429 only — retrying an idempotent-unsafe 4xx is how duplicates get created). CassetteMismatch when the tape drifts. verify_webhook(raw_body, signature, secret) — HMAC-SHA256 over RAW bytes, hmac.compare_digest.

gate.role: INBOUND · the merchant's half of agentic checkout

module.name: pkg/kavach/gate/envelope.py
module.envelope-fields: mandate_id, principal_id (the human delegating), agent_id, purpose (free text — what entailment scores against), merchant_allowlist, categories, per_txn_cap_minor, cumulative_cap_minor, not_before, not_after, nonce, issued_at.
module.failures: BAD_SIGNATURE · UNKNOWN_ISSUER · EXPIRED · NOT_YET_VALID · REPLAYED_NONCE · PRINCIPAL_MISMATCH · MALFORMED · REVOKED. Typed because "a bare False cannot be audited, explained to a merchant, or counted in an eval".
module.verify-order: 1. look up the issuer public key by key_id (unknown → UNKNOWN_ISSUER) 2. Ed25519 verify over the RAW BYTES, BEFORE parsing (verifying a round-tripped structure would make key order load-bearing and invite someone to "fix" it by relaxing the check) 3. parse (malformed → MALFORMED); `_minor` rejects bool/non-int/negative amounts 4. collect ALL of: not_before, not_after, principal binding, revocation 5. only if nothing failed, optionally CLAIM the nonce (INSERT OR IGNORE, rowcount==1) Claiming earlier would let anyone burn a legitimate mandate's nonce with a wrong clock or wrong principal — replay protection turned into a DoS primitive. claim_nonce=False makes it an INSPECTION: everything else is still checked, the mandate is not spent, and the answer therefore carries NO replay protection and must never gate money on its own. The Envelope is returned ONLY when nothing failed.

gate.module: Cart{cart_id, merchant_id, lines: tuple[CartLine]} · CartLine{sku, description, category, unit_amount_minor, quantity=1, liquid=False}. `total_minor` is DERIVED on both, never stored (a stored total can disagree with its lines, and the disagreement is what an attacker aims at). The price field is `unit_amount_minor`, not `amount_minor`, to stop a silent factor-of-quantity bug. The Cart is NOT a trust boundary: `category` and `liquid` are the MERCHANT'S catalogue facts, not claims by the arriving agent — which is exactly why they can be relied on. Violation = EMPTY_CART | MERCHANT_NOT_ALLOWED | CATEGORY_OUT_OF_SCOPE | PER_TXN_CAP_EXCEEDED | CUMULATIVE_CAP_EXCEEDED. admissible() returns ALL violations (a merchant debugging an integration should learn everything in one round-trip), is pure, and fails CLOSED on an empty category scope (an empty scope permits nothing, not everything). An empty cart is a malformed request wearing a pass, so it is a violation. spent(mandate_id) sums payload.total_minor over prior `gate.admitted` events — RECOMPUTED from the log on every call (ADR-016). record_admission() appends entity_type="mandate", event_type="gate.admitted", external_id=f"admission:{cart_id}" (so a retried admission counts once, inheriting eventlog's uniqueness), sig_verified=True (true here because verify() checked Ed25519).

score_drift(mandate_purpose, cart_text, untrusted_context) -> [0,1]. MECHANISM, stated exactly: word-set overlap (tokens > 3 chars, lowercased) between cart and untrusted context, MINUS the mandate purpose's own vocabulary, divided by |cart words|. Lexical, not learned. Measured cost: family F2 (goal drift) recall 0.550 — the weakest plane, and named as weakest rather than averaged into a headline. Safe to ship weak here ONLY because the score is advisory and can never authorise. explain_drift(): <0.2 nothing · <0.6 "minor correlation…" · else "high correlation …: goal drift detected".

check_velocity(conn, agent_id, now, window_seconds=3600) -> VelocityRisk. Counts rows in `intents` for that agent inside the window: >50 → score 1.0 "extreme velocity"; >20 → 0.6 "high velocity"; else 0.0. That is the WHOLE mechanism: there is no identity graph, no community detection and no GBM, and the module docstring says so rather than implying otherwise. Ring detection is the named upgrade path and needs columns the ledger does not have (device, address, token, principal), which is also why the function takes no principal_id — a parameter that changed nothing was removed.

module.name: pkg/kavach/gate/admission.py
module.verdicts: ALLOW · STEP_UP (re-consent from the principal — the buyer's side) · HOLD (merchant review — the merchant's side) · DENY. _CAUTION ranks ALLOW0 < STEP_UP1 < HOLD2 < DENY3 and is used ONLY to break expected-loss ties toward the safer option.
module.ladder: 1. envelope.verify() fails → DENY with the typed failures (nonce untouched) 2. mandate.admissible() violations → DENY with per-violation English reasons 3. model is None → STEP_UP. ALLOW is reachable ONLY through a model that actually read the cart: the deterministic layer cannot tell whether a perfectly in-scope, in-budget cart is what the principal asked for — that is the entire reason this plane exists (ADR-006/ADR-017). 4. risk = entailment model score; then FUSION, caution-only: risk = min(1.0, risk + provenance.score_drift(...)) risk = min(1.0, risk + population.check_velocity(...).score * 0.5) 5. verdict = argmin over expected_losses(), ties broken toward more caution.
module.expected-loss: Costs (merchant-supplied, every rate a STATED ASSUMPTION, reported with every result): fraud_loss_share=1.0 · margin_share=0.15 · step_up_minor=4_000 (₹40) · hold_minor=15_000 (₹150) · step_up_catch_rate=0.70 · hold_catch_rate=0.95 at_risk = cart_total * fraud_loss_share ALLOW = risk * at_risk STEP_UP = step_up_minor + risk * (1 - step_up_catch_rate) * at_risk HOLD = hold_minor + risk * (1 - hold_catch_rate) * at_risk DENY = (1 - risk) * cart_total * margin_share ← DENY is NOT free, which is why it cannot be the safe default.
module.where-the-nonce-is-spent: decide() verifies WITHOUT claiming the nonce and charges nothing — it is a genuine dry run, and calling it repeatedly costs nothing. admit() is the wrapper that, on ALLOW ONLY, claims the nonce (returning DENY/REPLAYED_NONCE if it was claimed concurrently) and calls mandate.record_admission() to charge the cumulative cap. A mandate is therefore single-use across ADMISSIONS, not across questions. admit() is the call a tool surface should make; decide() alone admits nothing.

intelligence.module: Model is a NamedTuple(vec: TfidfVectorizer, scaler: StandardScaler, clf: LogisticRegression, threshold=0.5, names: tuple[str,...], design_fn: Callable|None). Both `names` AND `design_fn` are needed for a second estimator to reuse the tuple — names alone would let an entailment model load without complaint and then score the wrong thing (pinned by tests/test_model.py). score(row) → P(class 1). explain(row, k=4) → per-decision attribution over STANDARDISED features (unscaled, log_time_gap sits near 9 for every row and swamps the attribution). save() persists a plain dict {vec, scaler, clf, threshold, names} — NOT the NamedTuple (pickling the class binds it to __main__ when trained as a script) and NOT design_fn (a pickled callable binds the artefact to an import path). load(path, design_fn=…) fails loudly on an artefact predating feature-name persistence. fit(train): TF-IDF (1,2)-grams, min_df=2, sublinear_tf, fitted on TRAIN text only; StandardScaler on relational features; LogisticRegression(max_iter=4000, class_weight="balanced"). Artefact: data/risk_model.pkl.

FEATURES = max_text_sim, dup_evidence, min_amount_delta, amount_exact_match, log_time_gap, frac_diff_session, n_prior, open_ratio, open_count, any_result_unknown, amount_share. `dup_evidence` = max over priors of similarity * (1 - amount_delta) — the duplicate signature. eligible(rows) keeps only rows with ≥1 prior intent on the same payment: the task is only DEFINED where a duplicate is possible, and scoring first-ever intents let an earlier model win by learning "does this payment have history" (ADR-014). Nothing reaches forward in time. design(): relational features (scaled) hstacked with TF-IDF of the reason TEXT itself. Text matters because "item arrived damaged" and "item arrived damaged - second unit in the same order" are highly similar to each other and to the prior, yet one is a duplicate and one is a separate obligation.

7 obligation kinds (duplicate_charge, item_damaged, shipping_fee, not_delivered, size_return, price_match, late_delivery), each with a share-of-payment range and 4–6 PARAPHRASES. Design constraints that make the eval mean anything: 1. duplicates are paraphrases, never string copies (otherwise exact equality wins); 2. hard negatives share payment, window and vocabulary and differ only in WHICH obligation they name — including a "second identical unit" negative with an IDENTICAL amount, so amount-matching cannot solve it; 3. duplicate amounts are deliberately NOT a reliable tell (same, re-decided slice, or a partial remainder); 4. the split is TEMPORAL and payment-disjoint, not random. DUPLICATE_RATE = 0.12 — a STATED ASSUMPTION, not a measurement; sensitivity is reported. `result_known` models the webhook-lag window (≈55% unknown). `python -m kavach.intelligence.corpus` writes data/intents.jsonl.

REVIEW_BUDGET = 0.20 of ELIGIBLE intents (≈11% of all agent traffic). Fixed-budget rather than cost-weighted because at ₹50 a review "escalate everything" is arithmetically cheapest and operationally absurd (ADR-014). Thresholds are chosen on TRAIN by quantile and frozen ("picking it on test is how benchmarks lie"). Baselines: B0 escalate everything · B1 exact text match · B2 rule amount+open+24h · B3 same learner blinded to text · B4 the shipped model. Reports precision, recall, AP, escalation rate, leaked rupees, plus the arithmetic recall ceiling at the budget and a 5/10/20/30% budget sweep. Hard asserts (these are the CI gate): within budget · AP > 0.75 · beats every feasible baseline on leaked rupees · text earns its place over B3. Writes data/risk_model.pkl (with the frozen threshold) and evals/risk_report.json.

Question: does the cart satisfy the PURPOSE the principal delegated? AP2, UPI Reserve Pay and Stripe Issuing all bound HOW MUCH a delegated agent may spend; none bounds WHAT IT MAY BUY. "weekly groceries under ₹2,000" is satisfied, to the rupee, by ₹1,800 of gift cards. FEATURES = purpose_sim_max, purpose_sim_mean, purpose_sim_value_weighted, unsupported_value_share, liquid_value_share, max_line_share, cap_utilisation, max_quantity, n_lines, log_total. `category_match_rate` is deliberately ABSENT: every cart reaching this model already passed admissible(), so it is the constant 1.0 — a column of no information and a misleading one to show a merchant. The PURPOSE STRING IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from the TF-IDF text block (only ten purpose archetypes exist in the corpus, so reading purposes directly would let the model memorise mandate identity). All purpose interaction is forced through the similarity features. Artefact: data/entailment_model.pkl; load() reattaches this module's design_fn.

28 catalogue items as (description, category, group, unit_minor, liquid); 10 mandates as (purpose, categories, cap, entailed groups). Categories are COARSE and purposes are FINE — the gap IS the thesis (a supermarket files gift cards under `grocery`). Attack families: F1_liquidity · F2_drift · F3_quantity · F4_cap_hugging. Negative families: N0_plain · N1_no_overlap (legit but zero lexical overlap) · N2_liquid_ok (a gift card the purpose asked for) · N3_near_cap · N4_many_lines — each defeats exactly one feature, so no single feature can decide the task. Constraints: every cart passes admissible() by construction; every attack ITEM and every attack SIGNATURE also appears legitimately; a failed draw returns None rather than clamping (clamping would make attack carts systematically cheaper and hand the model a free amount signal). VIOLATION_RATE = 0.15, a stated assumption. temporal_split drops any test mandate that appears in train.

STEP_UP_BUDGET = 0.20 of carts. Population: carts under a VALID envelope that already pass every deterministic check (ADR-014 in its Gate form). G0 step up everything · G1 lexical overlap · G2 category+cap rule (AP2/Reserve Pay/Stripe Issuing reduced to what they enforce — it flags NOTHING by construction, and that zero is the finding, not a strawman) · G3 hand-written red flags (liquid share, bulk quantity ≥5, ≥90% cap fill — the best rule an engineer writes without a model; ADR-011) · G4 same learner blinded to the cart's words · G5 the shipped model. Reports per-family recall and a budget sweep. Asserts: within budget · AP > 0.60 · beats every feasible baseline INCLUDING G3 ("if it cannot, the claim that purpose cannot be enforced by rules is wrong") · AP > G4 + 0.05. Note printed in the output: G1 and G3 exceed the budget because a rule with few distinct output values cannot be tuned to an arbitrary rate — a property of coarse rules, not a handicap imposed on them.

services.role: the single decision path; MCP, HTTP and the seeder all call these
services.module: Pipeline: intent → truth → exposure → duplicate risk → governor → record → event. risk_row(conn, intent, now) builds the estimator's feature row (priors = intents already recorded against the same target; nothing reaches forward in time). This lives here and nowhere else — it used to be inline in mcp/server.py, so an API wanting a score had to import a private helper or invent its own, and an invented one scores a different question under the same name. score_risk() returns (None, []) when there is no model — "not assessed", which the governor treats as a reason for caution, never a reason to proceed. With a model but no priors it returns (0.0, ["no prior intent on this target…"]) because the estimator is only defined where a duplicate is possible. evaluate(): decides WITHOUT writing anything (so the API has a genuine dry run and the adversary lab does not move the ledger). payment_captured is `rail_state == "CONFIRMED"`, and this is now the ONLY definition of "captured" in the tree. record(): SAVEPOINT-wrapped — governor.reserve() plus an eventlog append of `governor.decided.{allow|escalate|deny}` (entity_type="intent", parent = the target, sig_verified=False because it is OUR assertion, not a signed message from the rail). A decision recorded without its event, or vice versa, is a hole in the audit trail. evaluate_and_record(): the whole pipeline. It does NOT call Razorpay — execution is a separate deliberate step, which is precisely the state the reconciler exists to resolve.

overview(): exposure (open_minor/open_count/oldest_seconds), governed (intents, amount, executed, last_24h), refused (denied, escalated, protected_minor = amount on DENY+ESCALATE, duplicate_flagged = intents whose recorded decision carried duplicate_risk ≥ 0.5), review_queue, unresolved_outcomes, agents (active, admission_rate), integrity (chain verification + event count), by_status. Nothing is stored or seeded: "a metric that cannot go down is a decoration". stream(limit, before): the decision stream, newest first, CURSORED on created_at (offset paging would re-show or skip rows as the head moves).

listing/detail for payment|refund, obligations(), truth_trace(). Every row is a DERIVED fact — there is no payments table — so every response carries the event seqs it came from and a note saying "nothing here is a stored status field". truth_trace() re-derives after each event (rather than instrumenting derive()) so the derivation stays pure and the trace's last row IS the fact the governor read. It also ships the provenance vocabulary (observed / derived / inferred / policy) from the BACKEND so the frontend cannot relabel an inference as an observation.

listing (status/agent/target filters), review_queue, unresolved, get, agents(), agent_detail(), and detail() — ONE function assembling the seven things a dispute needs: the intent, the truth it was decided against, the risk scored, the governor's verdict, the provider outcome, the audit events, and proof they are intact. It is one call rather than seven endpoints because the VALUE is that the parts line up. Cited evidence is fetched by the seqs the decision RECORDED, not re-derived now — "a dispute is about what was known then".

act(conn, intent_id, action=approve|reject, reviewer, note). Approve moves ESCALATE → APPROVED and writes a `review.approved` event naming the reviewer; reject moves it to DENY. It NEVER calls Razorpay — putting a provider call behind an operator's click has a duplicate refund as its failure mode; an APPROVED intent with no result is the reconciler's job. Every response says `provider_call: "not attempted"` and what happens next, so the UI cannot imply money moved. A DENIED intent is NOT reviewable: DENY is an accounting invariant or a permission-tier refusal and no reviewer releases those. Idempotent on (intent, action) via the event log's (source, external_id) uniqueness — a double-clicked Approve is the most ordinary way to create a duplicate.

pack(intent_id) → a self-contained JSON artefact: subject, financial_truth, risk_assessment (labelled "advisory only"), governor_decision with the authority order, provider_outcome, audit_events, related_intents, proof (cited seqs, chain head, length, intact) and a `verification` block describing the hash recomputation EXACTLY, so a third party can re-verify without this codebase. JSON rather than PDF deliberately.

module.name: services/gate.py
module.role: inbound admission over HTTP + the demo principal

services.module: DEMO_KEY_ID = "kavach-demo-principal"; the Ed25519 private key is DERIVED from sha256(b"kavach/demo-principal/v1") — deterministic (a judge replaying a scenario gets byte-identical envelopes) and never stored on disk. register_demo_issuer() trusts its public half. What this is and is NOT: the signature check is REAL (a tampered envelope genuinely fails Ed25519); what it does not prove is that the mandate came from a real person — we minted it. Every response says so via `issuer.simulated: true`. sign(body) json.dumps(sort_keys, compact) → (raw bytes, signature); the raw bytes travel with the signature. admit(..., tamper=True) signs and THEN mutates the body (×100 on per_txn_cap_minor), so the forged-mandate scenario is genuinely forged rather than asserted. _stages() derives the 10-rung UI ladder (signature, issuer, validity, binding, revocation, replay, merchant, category, caps, purpose, admission) FROM WHAT THE DECISION PRODUCED — never a fixed list of ticks on a timer. A rung that was not reached says SKIPPED (a signature failure short-circuits parsing, so later envelope checks genuinely did not run); a missing model says UNAVAILABLE. inspect() verifies WITHOUT spending the nonce and returns the mandate plus spent/remaining and its prior admissions.

Every scenario builds its OWN in-memory SQLite, seeds at fixed epoch T = 1_700_000_000, and runs the REAL decision code. Deterministic (the judge's run matches ours) and isolated (the operator ledger cannot be inflated by the lab). Each scenario declares `expect` BEFORE running and reports outcome HELD | BROKEN | MODEL_UNAVAILABLE.
outbound-duplicate high expect ESCALATE|DENY needs_model duplicate refund across sessions outbound-over-refund critical expect DENY refund > captured amount (prompt-injected) outbound-unknown-state medium expect ESCALATE|DENY refund against an AMBIGUOUS obligation inbound-legitimate control expect ALLOW needs_model the gate must admit what it should inbound-category high expect DENY in-budget, out-of-scope (₹1,900 gold coin) inbound-cap high expect DENY per-transaction cap breach inbound-expired medium expect DENY lapsed mandate inbound-forged critical expect DENY cap raised after signing inbound-revoked high expect DENY revoked mandate on a stolen device inbound-replay high expect DENY needs_model one delegation spent twice inbound-goal-drift critical expect STEP_UP|HOLD|DENY needs_model injection → liquid value
Documented honesty in _outbound_duplicate's docstring: the estimator reads refund-reason TEXT so it is only meaningful on refund-shaped text (an earlier grocery-worded version scored 0.33 and the lab reported BROKEN), and it is sensitive to the gap between requests (at an 11-minute gap the same pair scores 0.46, under threshold — the deterministic layers still apply, but the model layer would let that one through). That limit is exactly why the model may only escalate. A scenario needing a model that is absent reports MODEL_UNAVAILABLE, not a pass.

mcp-surface.why: ADR-005: same tool names as Razorpay's MCP, different return type. Swapping is one line in an agent config — same tools, same arguments, same model, same prompt — so the A/B is fair. razorpay-mcp returns {"id":"rfnd_…","status":"processing"}; Kavach returns a decision, its reasons, and the events behind them.
mcp-surface.server-instructions: The MCPServer is constructed with instructions telling the agent that a refund with rail_state PROCESSING and obligation OPEN has NOT reached the customer, and to call list_open_obligations or check_refund before creating a refund.
mcp-surface.module-state: Opens KAVACH_DB at import (which is why it is transport, not logic), inits ledger + envelope schemas, constructs a Razorpay client and Policy, loads data/risk_model.pkl (setting Policy.risk_threshold to the model's frozen threshold) and data/entailment_model.pkl if present.
mcp-surface.tools:
payment as a FinancialFact + open_refund_exposure refund as a FinancialFact (processed ≠ credited) money in flight against a payment DRY RUN — the decision this refund WOULD get, computed by services.decisions.evaluate, i.e. the identical code create_refund runs. The thing the raw API cannot offer: you cannot ask Razorpay "would this be a duplicate?". Returns {"would", …decision, "truth", "dry_run": true}.
ingest payment if unknown → BEGIN EXCLUSIVE → decisions.evaluate → decisions.record (reserve + a hash-chained `governor.decided.*` event) → commit → (on ALLOW only) execute_provider outside the lock → ingest the resulting refund. intents held for a human, with reasons every intent against a payment and its outcome hash-chain verification inspect a mandate WITHOUT spending its nonce (base64 envelope + signature + key_id) — carries no replay protection by design full inbound admission; CONSUMES the nonce; on ALLOW charges the cumulative cap. Lines are {sku, description, category, amount (rupees per unit), quantity, liquid}; category and liquid come from the MERCHANT'S catalogue. (Read-only tools carry ToolAnnotations(read_only, non-destructive, idempotent); create_refund is annotated destructive and non-idempotent because a second call with a new intent is a second refund.)

http-api.boundary: The only thing the browser talks to. A typed shell over the same services the MCP surface uses — handlers validate, call ONE service function, and serialise. Any handler that starts making decisions belongs in pkg/kavach.
http-api.errors: Every failure leaves as {"error": {code, message, …}} — three handlers (HTTPException, RequestValidationError→422 with per-field problems, and a catch-all 500 that logs everything and discloses nothing but a reference id). One envelope, because two shapes means the client writes two code paths and the second renders "[object Object]".
http-api.db: One sqlite3 connection per request via a Depends contextmanager, opened with same_thread=False (FastAPI runs a sync dependency's body and its teardown on different threadpool threads, sequentially — never concurrently, and no connection is shared).
http-api.models: Loaded ONCE at startup; a model that fails to load stays absent rather than retrying per request, because absent widens caution, which is the safe direction.
http-api.static: If web/out exists it is mounted at "/" (html=True) so the demo is one process and one port with no CORS; a 404 serves the exported 404 page instead of Starlette's plain text. CORS allows only localhost:3000 and :4173 for the dev server.
http-api.endpoints: GET /api/health env truth: mode + note, db name, model availability, chain integrity, policy, ui flag GET /api/policy limits, threshold source, the 6-rung authority order, mutable:false + why GET /api/overview dashboard.overview GET /api/stream dashboard.stream (limit≤200, cursor `before`) GET /api/intents intents.listing (status/agent_id/target_id/limit/offset) GET /api/intents/{id} intents.detail — the unified decision view (404 intent_not_found) POST /api/governor/evaluate EvaluateRequest; dry run unless commit=true (SAME code path) GET /api/review intents.review_queue POST /api/review/{id} approve|reject → 404/409 mapped from ReviewError GET /api/reconciliation intents.unresolved GET /api/entities/{type} financials.listing; type ∈ (payment, refund) or 400 GET /api/entities/{type}/{id} financials.detail GET /api/truth/{type}/{id} financials.truth_trace (step-by-step derivation) GET /api/obligations financials.obligations GET /api/agents, /api/agents/{id} POST /api/gate/inspect verify a mandate without spending it POST /api/gate/admit full admission; body.commit=false leaves the nonce unclaimed GET /api/proof/chain windowed chain + status + claims GET /api/proof/verify full scan + claims GET /api/dispute/{id} dispute pack as a downloading JSON attachment GET /api/scenarios the catalogue + model availability POST /api/scenarios/{id}/run run one attack GET /api/evaluations evals/risk_report.json + evals/gate_report.json as written by CI GET /api/docs, /api/openapi.json
http-api.validation: Pydantic models with hard bounds: amounts are `int` bounded by MAX_MINOR_UNITS; identifiers ≤128 chars and REJECT control characters (they land in a log an operator reads, and a control char in one is an attempt to make a log line lie about its shape); ≤100 cart lines; untrusted_context ≤8000 chars.

frontend.stack: Next.js 16 (app router, output: export) · React 19 · TypeScript strict · GSAP · Lenis · motion · lucide-react
frontend.build: `next build` → web/out; trailingSlash:true so every route emits <route>/index.html (nothing resolves /dashboard to dashboard.html). NO assetPrefix — a relative prefix cannot be correct at two path depths at once, and it broke every console route's JS. Opening off disk degrades honestly (a `data-file` banner naming the command to run) rather than rendering blank.

surfaces.surface: A ten-chapter scroll narrative, defined once in web/lib/chapters.ts (used for render order, the "06 / 10" header readout, and the jump list): 01 THE COUNTER · 02 INTENT · 03 PRESSURE · 04 THE GRADIENT · 05 GOVERNOR · 06 EXECUTION · 07 RECONCILIATION · 08 EVIDENCE · 09 PROOF · 10 ENTER. Components: Smooth (one Lenis scroll authority driving GSAP), Chrome (spine/header/jump list — the spine is the append-only log at page scale and doubles as the progress bar), Hero, Divergence, Stage (three beats on one pinned canvas), Planes, Governor, Authority (a faithful port of governor.decide, including that _deny clears reasons), Stream (a faithful port of corpus.generate at 12%), ExpectedLoss (the admission argmin, playable), Execution + Reconcile, Evidence, Proof + ProofChain + Foot, Handoff (three doors: believe it / test it / verify it), Kinetic (word-level reveal).

Sidebar grouped by the QUESTION each group answers, not by entity type: Overview "What is happening?" → Command Centre, Decision Stream Money "What is actually true?" → Payments, Refunds, Obligations, Truth Explorer, Reconciliation Agents "Who is acting, and by whose authority?" → Agents, Agent Gate Authority "What is allowed, and what needs a human?" → Risk Intelligence, Governor, Review Queue Proof "Can we prove what happened?" → Proof & Audit Lab "Can we break it?" → Adversary Lab, Evaluations, Settings Routes on disk: adversary, agents, decisions, evaluations, gate, governor, obligations, overview, payments, proof, reconciliation, refunds, review, risk, settings, stream, truth. The environment badge reads /api/health, never a constant.

frontend.lib: api.ts — the ONLY place the app knows a backend exists. ApiError carries status/code/ fields/reference and a `remedy` sentence per status; a non-Kavach error shape (no {"error":…} envelope) is reported as unreachable, because that is what a static server with no API mounted actually is. NOTHING here invents data. useApi.ts — load/error/refresh + stale-response dropping. Deliberately not a state library: four needs, all of which fit in one file. format.ts — the ONLY place minor units become rupees. data.ts — everything the landing page ASSERTS, in one file, so tests/test_site.py can check it against evals/risk_report.json, governor.Policy, truth._STALE_SECONDS and the MCP tool decorators. ADR-007 does not stop at the edge of the repo. motion.ts / scroll.ts / useScene.ts / magnetic.ts / chapters.ts / util.ts — shared motion tokens and scroll primitives so nine sections cannot develop an accent; reduced-motion is honoured throughout. components/console/ui.tsx — the console's vocabulary of parts. Two carry meaning: <Why> (any refusal anywhere answers the same four questions in the same order) and <Ladder> (rungs rendered from what a decision produced; an unreached rung says SKIPPED rather than borrowing a tick from above).

DRIFT GUARD — parses web/lib/data.ts as text and checks the landing page's numbers and names against evals/risk_report.json, governor.Policy, truth._STALE_SECONDS and the MCP tool decorators. Costs CI no Node.
structural stylesheet rules (scoping/contrast), each of which was a real bug before it was a test
tests.gap: pkg/kavach/mcp/server.py has no test file — it opens a database at import, so it is exercised by hand. Everything it now calls (services/decisions) is covered.

adrs.note: condensed; read the file for the full text
adrs.adr: Transform Kavach v1 (payer-side UPI recovery) rather than keep or kill it; re-aim at the merchant side, where the naive consumer of a payment API is now an agent.
Build nothing that requires Vulcan — we have no access, so any prototype would measure a simulator we wrote ourselves.
Canonical states must be observable from Razorpay's position; NPCI-side conditions are AMBIGUOUS + a stated reason, never fabricated.
LLM placement: rules → ML → decision policy → LLM. The LLM narrates and disambiguates; it never determines state, amount, authorisation or duplicate risk.
Ship as an MCP server with Razorpay-compatible tool names — the deployment vector AND the reason the A/B is fair.
A wrong model may only widen caution. Model unavailable → confidence UNKNOWN → the policy floor rises to human approval.
No metric ships before its experiment (enforced into the frontend by test_site).
Concede idempotency keys, AP2 and Stripe explicitly in the README's first 200 words. The concession is the wedge: all of them bound a replay or an amount.
TRUTH is the headline; GOVERNOR is the delivery mechanism, not the pitch — caps and allowlists are being commoditised.
The semantic duplicate-risk model is P0 and load-bearing AI.
The baseline must be a STRONG baseline or the evaluation is worthless.
Submit to Track 05 (Open), written in Track 01's quality-bar vocabulary.
SQLite over Postgres+Redis+Docker; no torch; (originally) no React. Ceiling stated: SQLite is single-writer and will not survive production ingest.
Evaluate only where a duplicate is possible, at a FIXED review budget. Two methodology errors found by running the harness, not by reasoning about it.
Repository layout mirrors razorpay/razorpay-mcp-server (apps/ + pkg/ + Makefile + documents/), each choice traceable to a public Razorpay repo. Go-only conventions deliberately NOT transliterated.
Gate reuses the event log as its evidence spine; cumulative spend is recomputed, not counted. Ceiling stated: a scan per decision.
Entailment ships without an LLM (TF-IDF + relational features), measured at AP +0.351 over the blinded model; a missing model raises the floor to STEP_UP.
The first sixteen commits are a CURATED history and say so; each was exported to a clean tree and its own tests run there.
The landing page is a Next.js app; ADR-013's "no React" clause is narrowed to web/ only. `make check` and CI still run on Python alone.

kavach-context.threat-model: Trust boundaries, in order of strength: (1) the webhook HMAC — the security boundary of the whole system, and the only thing that produces DERIVED_CERTAIN confidence; (2) the Ed25519 delegation envelope over raw bytes; (3) the merchant's own catalogue (category/liquid are merchant facts, which is why they can be relied on); (4) everything an agent says, which is a claim and nothing more. Agent-supplied text (reason_text, cart descriptions, untrusted context) is treated as DATA scored by advisory models, never as instructions — the prompt-injection scenarios exist to demonstrate that an injected instruction cannot reach past an accounting invariant.

discrepancies.note: documentation vs code; the code is authoritative. The three that were open have been closed, and are kept here so the history stays legible.
discrepancies.d: The README used to advertise plane 4 "Population" as a "heterogeneous identity graph, community detection + GBM"; the implementation is, and always was, a velocity count. Fixed by making every claim match the code rather than by pretending to build a graph: pkg/kavach/gate/population.py now states the mechanism exactly and names what ring detection would need, the unused `principal_id` parameter is gone, and the README plane table, status table, mermaid diagram, "why AI is necessary" table and feature catalogue — plus web/lib/data.ts, which the landing page renders — now say "agent velocity" and mark ring detection as NOT built.

Fixed at the root rather than at the symptom. Two definitions of "captured" existed: services/decisions.evaluate used `rail_state == "CONFIRMED"` while mcp/server.check_refund used `not fact.obligation_open`, which also treats REVERSED / FAILED_TERMINAL / SETTLED payments as captured — so the dry run could ALLOW what the committed decision DENIED. Rather than patch the one expression, both MCP tools now call services/decisions: check_refund runs decisions.evaluate and create_refund runs decisions.evaluate + decisions.record. The duplicated `_risk`/`_payment_amount` helpers in mcp/server.py are deleted, so the tool surface can no longer hold its own opinion about what "captured" means or how a duplicate is scored. Side benefit: MCP-created decisions are now written into the hash-chained log as `governor.decided.*` events, which they previously were not — they only reached the mutable `intents.decision` column. Verified: on a REVERSED payment both check_refund and create_refund now return DENY.

admission.py's module docstring claimed decide() spends the nonce ("NOT SIDE-EFFECT FREE"), which stopped being true when the claim moved into admit(). Both the module docstring and decide()'s own docstring now state the real split: decide() verifies without claiming and charges nothing; admit() claims the nonce and charges the cumulative cap, and does both only on ALLOW.
reconciliation only understands tool="create_refund" / target_type="payment"; any other APPROVED intent is logged and left unresolved forever.

web/lib/data.ts still labels plane 3 Provenance `ai: 'learned'` at `~140 ms`, and plane 2 Intent at `~120 ms`. Provenance is lexical (its own module says so, and the README table says "Heuristic, advisory"), and apps/latency.py measures the WHOLE inbound path at p50 1.4 ms. The per-plane millisecond figures on the landing page are not measurements.

Self-declared ceilings, already documented but worth repeating for anyone reasoning about production use: SQLite single-writer with no Postgres adapter written; the WhatsApp/SMS step-up channel is not connected (the decision and its audit record are produced, sending is one adapter); NPCI UAP and UPI Reserve Pay have no public API, so the Ed25519 envelope is a field-for-field stand-in; both corpora are synthetic; the 12% duplicate base rate and all four Costs rates are STATED ASSUMPTIONS; precision 0.813 means ~1 in 5 escalations delays a legitimate refund; Gate F2 (goal drift) recall is 0.550.

working-notes.audience: an LLM about to modify this repo
working-notes.n: Put decision logic in pkg/kavach/services/ or lower. A FastAPI handler or an MCP tool that starts deciding creates the second decision path this codebase is organised to prevent — and that is exactly how the two definitions of "captured" appeared.

Never let a learned score make an outcome less cautious. If a change would let a model turn ESCALATE into ALLOW or DENY into anything, it violates ADR-006 and tests/test_governor.py and tests/test_admission.py will catch it — but the design intent matters more than the test.
Never store a derived number. If you find yourself adding a counter column for cumulative spend or open exposure, read ADR-016 first.
Any new money field is an integer named `*_minor`, parsed by money.parse_inr at the boundary, and formatted only in web/lib/format.ts.

Any new event must go through eventlog.append with a deterministic external_id, so replay is idempotent, and must set sig_verified=True ONLY when a real signature was checked (webhook HMAC or Ed25519 envelope). Our own assertions are sig_verified=False.
Any new verdict, reason string or state must be citable: emit the event seqs behind it. Reasons are templated from the evidence chain deliberately so they cannot hallucinate.

Do not describe a mechanism as more than it is. Two planes here are heuristics (provenance, population) and say so in their own docstrings; if you strengthen one, measure it in the benchmark before any document says so (ADR-007).
If you change a benchmark number, governor.Policy, a truth staleness tolerance, an enum member or an MCP tool name, tests/test_site.py will fail until web/lib/data.ts agrees.
`make bench` and `make gate-bench` are ASSERTING benchmarks and run in CI: a model quality regression breaks the build like a failing test.

The demo seed (apps/demo_data.py) anchors to wall time on purpose. A fixed epoch made every seeded refund age past the 6-hour staleness tolerance and show as AMBIGUOUS. The Adversary Lab, by contrast, keeps a fixed epoch T=1_700_000_000 because a judge reproducing an attack must get byte-identical output.
